newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Murder still considered in Menem son's death.
newsitem.headline: Murder still considered in Menem son's death.

text.p: A judge probing the death of Argentine President Carlos Menem's son has included in the files a document stating that murder was still a possibility, yet Menem insisted on Tuesday his death was an accident.

Menem's estranged wife Zulema Yoma showed CBS-Telenoticias TV network a judge's certificate dated March 18 that said elements in the investigation of Carlos Jr.'s death in a helicopter crash two years ago pointed to possible foul play.
"The investigation ... points to the possibility of double murder," the document said.

The 26-year-old was killed in March 1995 with his friend Silvio Oltra when the helicopter Carlos Jr. was piloting crashed. An autopsy performed last year following an exhumation requested by Yoma concluded there was no foul play and the probe has been conducted as if it were an "accident."
In a separate interview, Menem insisted he did not believe in the murder theory. "The information I have is ... that it was an accident," he said.
Menem also said a former security agent's remarks that there was a third person in the helicopter in which his son was killed was "a shame" and "a lie."

Last week former security agent Jorge Artony said he had heard security chief Brigadier Andres Antonietti say at the time of the crash that there had been a third person aboard. His remarks followed unconfirmed reports about a young blond woman aboard the craft at the time of takeoff.
Yoma, who has insisted all along on the murder theory and has recently asked Pope John Paul for help, said on Tuesday, "There are many indications that there was a third person."

She suspects Carlos Jr. was the victim of dirty politics or drug trafficking and has accused Menem of a covering up. Her lawyers said they will request Judge Carlos Villafuerte to call Antonietti and other witnesses to testify.
